question.worked_solution:
The first thing we notice is that we can rewrite the terms of the series as powers of $\frac{2}{7}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}1-\frac{2}{7}+\frac{4}{49}-⋯+\frac{(-1)^{n}\,{2}^{n}}{{7}^{n}}+⋯ & =1-\frac{2}{7}+\frac{{2}^{2}}{{7}^{2}}+⋯+(-1)^{n}\frac{{2}^{n}}{{7}^{n}}+⋯ \\  & =1-\frac{2}{7}+{(\frac{2}{7})}^{2}+⋯+(-1)^{n}{(\frac{2}{7})}^{n}+⋯\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we recognize that the series looks similar to the Maclaurin expansion for $f(x)=\frac{1}{1+x}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{1+x} & =1-x+{x}^{2}-{x}^{3}+⋯+(-1)^{n}{x}^{n}+⋯\,\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $x=\frac{2}{7}$ into our Maclaurin expansion gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{(1+\frac{2}{7})} & =1-\frac{2}{7}+{(\frac{2}{7})}^{2}-{(\frac{2}{7})}^{3}+⋯+(-1)^{n}{(\frac{2}{7})}^{n}+⋯ \\ \frac{7}{9} & =1-\frac{2}{7}+\frac{4}{49}-\frac{8}{343}+⋯+\frac{(-1)^{n}\,{2}^{n}}{{7}^{n}}+⋯\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the sum of the series is $\frac{7}{9}.$
